summary: Validated Apple Sign-In server-side identity token verification flow (/api/auth/apple) and confirmed no regressions on existing endpoints. All 5 existing pytest unit tests pass (mocked JWKS) and 14 new curl-style regression tests pass against the live preview URL. Apple verification properly rejects missing/invalid/wrong-audience/expired tokens with appropriate 401/422 codes, and the unit test confirms creating a new user + re-login with same Apple sub resolves to same user_id with preserved email/name.

minor.issue: When given a completely non-JWT string (e.g. 'not.a.jwt'), the error message is 'Unable to verify Apple sign-in' (from the JWKS lookup step) rather than 'Invalid Apple sign-in token'. Both contain 'Apple' so existing tests pass and behaviour is acceptable, but a unified 'Invalid Apple sign-in token' for all malformed inputs would be cleaner UX.
Using deprecated @app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown') — should migrate to FastAPI lifespan event handlers (DeprecationWarning emitted on every test run).

critical_code_review_comments: Apple identity token verification (server.py lines 193-222) correctly validates ES256 signature against JWKS, checks audience=APPLE_BUNDLE_ID, checks issuer=https://appleid.apple.com, and handles expired/invalid token cases with distinct HTTP 401 messages — matches Apple's recommended server-side verification flow.
User lookup by apple_sub first then email (lines 247-249) is the correct precedence — Apple sub is stable across name/email changes.

Synthesized fallback email f'{apple_sub}@privaterelay.appleid.com' (line 272) is sensible for cases where Apple withholds email, but worth verifying there's no unique-index conflict if user_email already has that exact value (edge case).
Bearer token support in /api/auth/me (lines 311-313) is correct and necessary for native iOS clients — addressed in review request.
Cookie attrs samesite='none' + secure=True are appropriate for cross-origin native usage. httponly=True is correct.
Minor: _apple_jwk_client global cache is module-level; if Apple rotates JWKS we depend on PyJWKClient's internal TTL refresh, which is fine in practice.
Minor: server.py is 1203 lines — exceeds 700-line guideline; consider splitting auth/AI/tracker into separate routers.
Deprecated @app.on_event handlers (startup/shutdown) — migrate to lifespan handlers.
test_credentials: N/A — Apple Sign-In flow does not use stored test credentials. Unit tests mock JWKS with a generated ES256 keypair to produce valid tokens for backend verification. /app/memory/test_credentials.md does NOT exist.
seed_data_creation: None. Unit tests create + clean up users with apple_sub prefix '001.test.*' after each test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Apple Sign-In endpoint /api/auth/apple is fully validated: 5 mocked-JWKS unit tests in /app/backend/tests/test_apple_auth.py (rejection of missing/invalid/wrong-aud/expired tokens; create-user-then-relogin flow) + 14 live-URL regression tests in /app/backend/tests/test_apple_auth_curl.py. Server config: APPLE_BUNDLE_ID=com.peptrackpro.app, JWKS=https://appleid.apple.com/auth/keys, ISSUER=https://appleid.apple.com. Cookie + body session_token issued. Bearer token accepted on /api/auth/me. NOTE: When running async tests across multiple files with motor, you'll hit 'Event loop is closed' due to motor caching loop reference — this is test infra only, not a production bug. Run async test files individually if needed.
rca of the issue: N/A — no production bugs found. The endpoint correctly addresses Apple App Store Guideline 2.1(a) rejection by performing real server-side ES256 JWT verification against Apple's JWKS, upserting user by stable apple_sub, and returning session_token in both cookie and response body so native iOS clients (which can't always persist cookies) can use Authorization: Bearer on subsequent requests.
